title: Reflection's Beam aims to undercut Chinese open models with fewer tokens, not cheaper tokens
source_used: SiliconANGLE (own reporting), Unite.AI (relaying Reflection and Baseten announcements), AWS Machine Learning Blog (Reflection partner post); the VentureBeat original returned HTTP 429 and was not opened
key_facts: Reflection AI, a US start-up, made the weights of Beam, its first large language model, available on Hugging Face on 16 Oct 2026, with training recipes and tools to customize and measure the model (SiliconANGLE).

Beam is a mixture-of-experts model with 501 billion total and 23 billion active parameters, released under the Apache 2.0 license in BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 versions, plus a drafter model for speculative decoding (Unite.AI; AWS blog).

Reflection says it trained Beam to solve coding and agent tasks while using fewer tokens, with long reinforcement-learning rollouts and a length penalty; a reasoning-effort setting lets users trade shorter answers for deeper thinking (Baseten launch post, as relayed by Unite.AI).
Benchmark scores quoted come from Reflection's own evaluations, for example 90.5% on GPQA Diamond and 80.9% on SWE-bench Verified (Unite.AI, citing Baseten).
Reflection first introduced Beam on 5 Oct 2026, when early access was limited to a waitlist and weights were promised later in the month (Unite.AI).
Reflection plans more training recipes (self-distillation) in the coming days (SiliconANGLE; Unite.AI).
Launch platforms named include Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Cloudflare, Databricks, Vercel, Ollama and OpenRouter (Unite.AI).
quote_evidence: Startup Reflection AI Inc. today made the weights of Beam, its first large language model, available on Hugging Face.
Reflection releases Beam’s weights through Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 license.
Baseten said Reflection trained Beam to solve coding and agentic tasks while using fewer tokens
why_it_matters_hint: Anyone can now download and test a US-built open model that Reflection says competes with Chinese ones; the performance claims rest on Reflection's own evaluations.
notes: VentureBeat page blocked (HTTP 429). Same news read at SiliconANGLE (16 Oct 2026), Unite.AI and the AWS blog. Unite.AI labels its author as an AI-generated research agent, so its details are attributed to Reflection or Baseten and the 501B size, 23B active size and Apache 2.0 license were cross-checked against the AWS blog. Nvidia backing and the 5 Oct unveiling come from our own 5 and 6 Oct 2026 editions.
